title: Release 2.4.0: the catalog API restarts in a loop

lines.text: 14:10 monitor: catalog.fernhill.example answers 502; catalog-api restarted 6 times since the 14:08 release
partner-feed: catalog pull failed; partner marks Fernhill titles unavailable until the next pull

nodes.label: catalog-api
nodes.status: {up ? (running == "rollback" ? "Running 2.3.9 (rolled back)" : running == "tsx" ? "Running 2.4.0 under npx tsx" : "Running 2.4.1") : "Exits with code 1 at startup; restarting"}

objective: Run TypeScript with Node.js type stripping, and recognize the syntax it rejects
secondaryObjectives: Choose a union of string literals or an as const object over an enum when code must stay erasable

sources.cite: Node.js v26 API, Modules: TypeScript (type stripping)
sources.note: Key values used (read in full as raw HTML on 2026-11-14 for the TSNODE course, REQ-267, and carried on its unit sources): type stripping is on by default and stable, runs files that use only erasable syntax, does no type checking and ignores tsconfig.json; enums, runtime namespaces, parameter properties and import aliases raise ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX. Not re-read for this sim. The exact error text in the scenario's journal, and the tsc message, are authored renderings; only the error code ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX is the source's.

Key value used (read in full as raw HTML on 2026-11-14 for the TSNODE course, REQ-267): erasableSyntaxOnly makes enums, parameter properties and runtime namespaces errors, so tsc reports what Node.js type stripping would refuse. Not re-read for this sim.

Key value used (read on 2026-11-14 for the TSNODE course, REQ-267): an enum generates JavaScript at run time, so Node.js type stripping rejects it; a union of string literals or an as const object is erasable. Not re-read for this sim.

brief.situation: You are the on-call engineer at Fernhill Books, a fictional online bookshop. catalog-api runs its TypeScript directly with Node.js 26 type stripping (node src/server.ts, no build step). Release 2.4.0 went out at 14:08; since then the service exits at startup, systemd restarts it, and the catalog pages answer 502. A partner store pulls the catalog at 14:35 and marks every title unavailable if the pull fails. Restore the service, fix what broke, and make sure the next release cannot break it the same way.
handover: CI runs tsc --noEmit on every pull request, and 2.4.0 passed it.
Releases are tagged; a rollback to the previous tag takes about 3 minutes, a new release about 6.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The incident keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, service or job and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command or change takes, and when the fictional incident develops, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The partner pull at 14:35 is 25 minutes after the first alert.

writeup.question: For the incident record: why a release that passed tsc would not start, how you restored it, and what stops this class of break next time.

parts.label: Why it would not start
parts.criteria: Explains that Node.js type stripping only removes type syntax and refuses syntax that generates JavaScript, such as an enum (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX), and that tsc accepts enums, so the type check could not catch it.
parts.modelAnswer: 2.4.0 added an enum. Type stripping erases types and nothing else; an enum compiles to a runtime object, so Node.js refused the file with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX and the process exited 1. tsc --noEmit passed because an enum is valid TypeScript.

parts.label: Restoring service
parts.criteria: Rolls back or ships an erasable replacement (an as const object with a union type) quickly; does not keep restarting the same release or swap the production runtime for an unreviewed loader.
parts.modelAnswer: I rolled back to 2.3.9 within minutes, then shipped 2.4.1 with OrderStatus as an as const object and a string-literal union, which strips cleanly.

parts.label: Prevention
parts.criteria: Turns on erasableSyntaxOnly so tsc in CI rejects non-erasable syntax, and prefers unions or as const objects over enums.
parts.modelAnswer: tsconfig now has erasableSyntaxOnly, so CI's tsc fails on an enum, a parameter property or a runtime namespace; the team uses unions and as const objects instead.

scoring.modelReasoning: Node.js type stripping runs .ts files by removing type syntax only; an enum generates a runtime object, so Node.js refuses the file with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX and the process exits 1. tsc accepts enums, which is why CI passed. Roll back to restore service fast, then replace the enum with an as const object and a string-literal union, and turn on erasableSyntaxOnly so tsc rejects non-erasable syntax before release.
